paragraphs: Yudhishthira, a disciple of Krishna and once the emperor of India, lost his kingdom to his enemies. He had to flee with his queen and live in a forest in the Himalayas.
One day the queen asked him a painful question. He was the most virtuous man she knew. Why, then, should he have to suffer so much?

Yudhishthira pointed to the mountains around them. Look how grand and beautiful they are, he said. They give him nothing, yet he loves them, simply because it is his nature to love what is grand and beautiful. In the same way he loved the Lord, the source of all beauty and greatness. He did not pray for anything or ask for anything in return. God could put him wherever He wished; his love would stay the same.
He ended with words that sum up the whole story: "I cannot trade love."
learn: When life is unfair, it is tempting to treat goodness like a bargain that has failed. Yudhishthira shows another way: be good and love what is worth loving because that is who you are, not because of what it will get you.
